title: The Lipschitz Constant of Self-Attention
authors: Hyunjik Kim; George Papamakarios; Andriy Mnih
evidence: P01; full original focal reading §3.1–3.2, Eq8, Theorem3.2
application: Character-level language modelling and invertible self-attention
established_mechanism: L2 pairwise attention with tied query/key maps and a theoretical Lipschitz bound; ordinary dot-product attention has an unbounded-domain pathology.
candidate_difference: One learned pooling query plus a causal discrepancy penalty and radial saturation of values differs structurally from its pairwise L2 score. Exact novelty of that combination remains unestablished. The radial saturation itself equals the gradient of a pseudo-Huber-shaped radial penalty; that ingredient is not claimed new. Its specific historical primary source was not verified here.
remaining: Full comparison including appendices and later robust-attention papers; no Bitcoin sigma7 advantage established.

title: Lipschitz Normalization for Self-Attention Layers with Application to Graph Neural Networks
authors: George Dasoulas; Kevin Scaman; Aladin Virmaux
evidence: P02 original focal reading §4–5, Theorem3, Eqs15/17/19; P03 author README
application: Graph node classification; deep GAT and Graph Transformer
established_mechanism: Scores normalized using norms of inputs and queries; a learned query and Lipschitz attention are already explicit prior art.
candidate_difference: The candidate bounds the values through a smooth radial map and adds a causal disagreement term instead of applying the paper score normalization. These ingredients need novelty review beyond this pairwise comparison. The radial saturation itself equals the gradient of a pseudo-Huber-shaped radial penalty; that ingredient is not claimed new. Its specific historical primary source was not verified here.
remaining: The label Lipschitz or a learned query cannot be the novelty claim. No implementation was copied.

title: TimeMixer: Decomposable Multiscale Mixing for Time Series Forecasting
evidence: P04 author README; inherited E2 §5 review, not a new full-paper reading
application: General multivariate and univariate series forecasting
established_mechanism: MLP past-decomposable mixing and future multipredictor mixing over scales.
candidate_difference: The candidate uses a fixed causal average inside an attention penalty rather than TimeMixer PDM/FMM. The E2 ETTh1 calendar defect does not establish a BTC limitation solved by this mechanism.
remaining: Quantify a BTC-specific limitation in development; neither multiscale processing nor its generic use is new.
